newsitem.title: CANADA: Edper shares rise on merger news.
newsitem.headline: Edper shares rise on merger news.

text.p: Shares in Edper Group Ltd climbed on Friday on news it will merge with its brother company, Hees International Bancorp Inc.
In contrast, Hees shares sank in moderate trading.
"The arbs (arbitrageurs) are buying Edper and shorting the Hees," said one trader.
Edper class A shares rose 0.65 to 6.00 in relatively active trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange while Hees shares sank 0.60 to 16.20 in quiet dealings.
The proposed holding company merger is designed to untangle the complex web that is the Edper-Bronfman group.
Under the deal, holders of Edper class A non-voting and class B voting shares will receive 0.38 shares of the amalgamated company for each Edper Group share.
Hees shareholders will receive one share of the new company for every Hees share held.
Given that Hees was trading around C$16.20 mid-morning on the TSE, the value of 0.38 of the merged company share is around C$6.16 or 38 percent of a Hees share.
Edper Group receipts were up 9.80 at 61.50 in turnover of 4.21 million shares.
Dominion Bond Rating Service confirmed Hees' debt and preferred share ratings in light of the proposed union.

"The confirmation is based on the proposed amalgamation receiving the necessary support, with little change in the terms and conditions. The proposal continues the process of simplifying the corporate structure of the Edper-Hees group begun several years earlier," DBRS said.
The agency said the capital structure of the new company will be very similar to that of the original Hees since the Edper Group's main asset is simply an investment in Hees.
